newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Islamic Bank chief wants to support private sector.
newsitem.headline: Islamic Bank chief wants to support private sector.

text.p: The head of the Islamic Development Bank said on Saturday the bank wanted to give more support to the private sector in its member states.

Ahmed Mohamed Ali told a news conference the bank was financing the participation of 12 small and medium-sized firms from Tunisia, Jordan, Egypt, Saudi Arabia, Algeria and Morocco at the Tunis Trade Fair which opened on Friday.
"We are now focusing on supporting the private sector after having dealt in the past with only the public sector," Mohamed Ali said.
"We want to give these firms the opportunity to make their products known in an effort to boost trade between Moslem countries," he added.
He also attended on Saturday a bank-sponsored symposium on trade exchanges between Moslem countries.

Tunisian Prime Minister Hamed Karoui on Friday opened the fair with 396 exhibitors taking part from 38 foreign countries, including 72 firms from Egypt and 66 from Syria. The fair closes on October 24.
